changelog: **Mail delivery: lane rules and a shared send budget, observe mode (#2941):** the pure `src/lib/mailDeliveryRule.ts` reads the lane of every mail (CRITICAL / TRANSACTIONAL / BULK) from the `emailGroups` taxonomy only, classifies an SMTP failure (a relay throttle, a connection/auth failure or any refusal before the message — greeting, EHLO, STARTTLS, AUTH, MAIL FROM — is relay-wide; another 4xx retries the message; a 5xx, or a message nodemailer itself refuses, is final), and holds the backoff, the GCRA tolerance with a critical reserve, the throttle pause ladder and natural de-duplication keys (unit-tested with a coverage floor). A new `MailBudget` table (no `orgId`, operational like `JobLease`) is the meter, one row per SMTP channel (`smtp`, and `smtp:bulk` for the optional bulk server, with optional `MAIL_BULK_*` numbers), and `src/lib/mailBudgetStore.ts` spends a token with one conditional UPDATE on `UTC_TIMESTAMP(3)`. `sendEmail()` is split into `prepareEmail()` + `sendPrepared()`/`deliverPrepared()` with its signature and behaviour unchanged; a pooled drain transport and a short-timeout urgent transport exist but are not used yet. With `MAIL_METER_MODE=observe` (the default; `off` disables) the meter (`src/lib/mailMeterObserver.ts`) runs beside every real send — one meter statement at a time per process, a bounded backlog — and logs `mail_meter.would_refuse` with the lane, channel and wait, but never refuses or delays a mail. `EmailStatus.DEFERRED` is added (nothing writes it yet) and the e-mail health read reports `deferred24h`. `.env.example` documents `MAIL_RATE_PER_MIN`, `MAIL_BURST`, `MAIL_URGENT_RESERVE` and `MAIL_METER_MODE` with recommended values per environment.
